properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.autowired-enabled
properties.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.bridge-error-handler
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.channel-properties
properties.description: The JGroups XML configuration of the JChannel that each endpoint creates, as a file, a URL or a classpath resource. If not set, the raft.xml in the camel-jgroups-raft JAR is used, and a WARN is logged when an endpoint starts. That raft.xml is a sample for development and tests: it uses UDP multicast without authentication or encryption, and lists A as the only RAFT member. In production, set your own configuration, with AUTH and SYM_ENCRYPT or ASYM_ENCRYPT, and the members of the cluster in the members attribute of RAFT. Not used when the raftHandle option is set.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the jgroups-raft component. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.lazy-start-producer
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.raft-handle
properties.description: To use a custom org.jgroups.raft.RaftHandle for all the endpoints of this component. When set, the raftId, channelProperties and stateMachine options are not used. The component closes its channel and its log when the component stops. The option is a org.jgroups.raft.RaftHandle type.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.raft-id
properties.description: The Raft ID of this member, which also names the JChannel. A member whose ID is not in the members attribute of RAFT in the channel configuration is a Learner, which does not vote. If not set, the raft_id of the channel configuration is used. Not used when the raftHandle option is set.

properties.name: camel.component.jgroups-raft.state-machine
properties.description: The org.jgroups.raft.StateMachine that applies the committed log entries, for the RaftHandle that each endpoint creates. The default NopStateMachine ignores the entries and returns an empty byte array. Not used when the raftHandle option is set. The option is a org.jgroups.raft.StateMachine type.
